hooks.text: The fastest object ever launched from Earth carried a postage stamp.
Earth's fastest launched deep space probe carried a postage stamp.
Why did the fastest launched probe carry an ordinary postage stamp?

title: The Fastest Probe Ever Launched Carried a Stamp
description: NASA launched New Horizons as the fastest mission ever sent from Earth, carrying a 1991 stamp that dared them to explore Pluto.

beats.text: The fastest object ever launched from Earth carried a postage stamp.
beats.visual: New Horizons spacecraft in the cleanroom during launch preparations, 2005
queries: New Horizons probe Kennedy Space Center

beats.text: On January 19, 2006, NASA launched New Horizons directly into an escape trajectory.
beats.visual: Atlas V rocket launching the New Horizons spacecraft, 2006

beats.text: It reached an Earth-relative speed of 16.26 kilometers per second, setting the launch record.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the New Horizons probe escaping Earth orbit, 2006
queries: New Horizons spacecraft trajectory artist concept

beats.text: In 2007, a Jupiter gravity assist added roughly four kilometers per second of speed.
beats.visual: New Horizons image of volcanic eruption on Jupiter's moon Io, 2007

beats.text: Astronomers used the ALMA radio telescope array in Chile to precisely measure Pluto's orbit.
beats.visual: Antenna dishes of the ALMA radio observatory on the Chajnantor plateau, 2015

beats.text: On July 14, 2015, New Horizons became the first spacecraft to study Pluto up close.
beats.visual: High-resolution color photograph of Pluto captured by New Horizons, 2015

beats.text: The probe flew past at over 52,000 miles per hour carrying nine cultural mementos.
beats.visual: High-resolution photograph of Pluto's moon Charon taken by New Horizons, 2015

beats.text: Among them was a 1991 postage stamp printed with 'Pluto: Not Yet Explored.'
beats.visual: The 1991 US Postal Service stamp reading Pluto Not Yet Explored, 1991

beats.text: After roughly 9.5 years, that probe finally delivered the stamp to its destination.
beats.visual: Diagram showing New Horizons trajectory past Pluto through the Kuiper Belt, 2015

better_than_last: Replaces biographical and catalog listings with immediate launch velocity records and a seamless narrative loop back to the opening stamp hook, directly addressing ep111 and ep114 learnings.
